final_answer:
**Yes, two of the five CAPAs share an upstream cause: the INC-03 incubator door.**

- **CAPA-26-012** (OPEN, owner Engineering, change control CC-26-019) comes from **DEV-26-011**, an OQ test incident. The door-open alarm on INC-03 activated at 142 s against a limit of 60 s. The recorded root cause is "Door switch misaligned" (equipment component).
- **CAPA-26-015** (CLOSED, owner Manufacturing, effectiveness check still PENDING) comes from **DEV-26-033**, a PPQ26-02 protocol deviation. Harvest viability fell below the PPQ-001 criterion of 80%, and INC-03's door was found not fully latched on 11-Jun. The recorded root cause is "Operator did not confirm door latch per SOP-MFG-105" (human error).

The two recorded root causes differ, but both deviations trace to INC-03's door closure. The trace links for both deviations point to INC-03, and the equipment log has ALM-DOOR alarms on INC-03 on 10-Jun. The CAPAs address the door hardware (switch replacement) and the operator check (retraining), so one fix may not close the other. The link is inferred from the shared equipment and the descriptions, not from a common root cause recorded in the system.

The other three CAPAs have no shared cause with these:
- CAPA-26-008 (FRZ-80-02 compressor) is a standalone equipment failure.
- CAPA-26-019 (tubing sampling-port weld) is a supplier defect.
- CAPA-26-016 (CD3% acceptance criterion, from DEV-26-027) rests on a donor-variability root cause. The apheresis CD3% for ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 was 65.3% and 63.8%, which does not support low CD3 as the cause. I did not find a shared upstream cause for it, but the root cause looks questionable and may deserve a separate look.
